source_text: Ἰουδαῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ νῦν διδάσκουσι τὸν ἀνωνόμαστον θεὸν λελαληκέναι τῷ Μωυσεῖ. Ὁθεν τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα διὰ Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προμεμηνυμένου προφήτου ἐλέγχον αὐτούς, ὡς προεγράψαμεν, εἶπεν· „Ἔγνω βοῦς τὸν κτησάμενον καὶ ὄνος τὴν φάτνην τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ, Ἰσραὴλ δέ με οὐκ ἔγνω καὶ ὁ λαός με οὐ συνῆκε“. Καὶ Ἰησοῦς δὲ ὁ Χριστός, ότι οὐκ ἔγνωσαν Ἰουδαῖοι, τί πατὴρ καὶ τί υἱός, ὁμοίως ἐλέγχων αὐτοὺς καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν· „Οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱός, οὐδὲ τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν ἀποκαλύψῃ ὁ υἱός“. Ὁ λόγος δὲ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν. Καὶ ἄγγελος δὲ καλεῖται καὶ ἀπόστολος· αὐτὸς γὰρ ἀπαγγέλλει, ὅσα δεῖ γνωσθῆναι, καὶ ἀποστέλλεται μηνύσων, ὅσα ἀγγέλλεται, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἱ κύριος ἡμῶν εἶπεν· „Ὁ ἐμοῦ ἀκούων ἀκούει τοῦ ἀποστείλαντός με“. Καὶ ἐκ τῶν τοῦ Μωϋσέως δὲ συγγραμμάτων φανερὸν τοῦτο γενήσεται. Λέλεκται δὲ ἐν αὐτοῖς οὕτως· „Καὶ ἐλάλησε Μωϋσεῖ ἄγγελος θεοῦ ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς ἐκ τῆς βάτου καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, θεὸς Ἀβραάμ, θεὸς Ἰσαάκ, θεὸς Ἰακώβ, ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου. Κάτελθε εἰς Αἰγυπτον καὶ ἐξάγαγε τὸν λαόν μου“. Τὰ δ᾿ ἑπόμενα ἐξ ἐκείνων βουλόμενοι μαθεῖν δύνασθε· οὐ γὰρ δυνατὸν ἐν τούτοις ἀναγράψαι πάντα. Ἀλλ᾿ εἰς ἀπόδειξιν γεγόνασιν οἵδε οἱ λόγοι, ότι υἱὸς θεοῦ καὶ ἀπόστολος ᾿Ιησοῦς ὁ Χριστός ἐστι, πρότερον λόγος ὤν, καὶ ἐν ἰδέᾳ πυρὶ ς ποτὲ φανείς, ποτὲ δὲ καὶ ἐν εἰκόνι ἀσωμάτῳ· νῦν δὲ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἀνθρωπείου γένους ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος ὑπέμεινε καὶ παθεῖν, ὅσα αὐτὸν ἐνήργησαν οἱ δαίμονες διατεθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνοήτων Ἰουδαίων. Οἵτινες ἔχοντες ῥητῶς εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς Μωϋσέως συντάγμασι· „Καὶ ἐλάλησεν ἄγγελος τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ Μωϋσεῖ ἐν πυρὶ φλογὸς ἐν βάτῳ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ἱ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ“, τὸν τῶν όλων πατέρα καὶ δημιουργὸν τὸν ταῦτα εἰπόντα λέγουσιν εἶναι. Ὅθεν καὶ τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα ἐλέγχον αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· „Ἰσραὴλ δέ με οὐκ ἔγνω, καὶ ὁ λαός με οὐ συνῆκε“. Καὶ πάλιν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ὡς ἐδηλώσαμεν, παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς ἂν εἶπεν· „Οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα εἰ μἰ ὁ υἱός, οὐδὲ τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν ἱ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψῃ“. Ἰουδαῖοι οὖν ἡγησάμενοι ἀεὶ τὸν πατέρα τᾶν ὅλων λελαληκέναι τῷ Μωϋσεῖ, τοῦ λαλήσαντος αὐτῷ ὄντος υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἄγγελος καὶ ἀπόστολος κέκληται, δικαίως ἐλέγχονται καὶ διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς οὔτε τὸν πατέρα οὔτε τὸν υἱὸν ἔγνωσαν. Οἱ γὰρ τὸν υἱὸν πατέρα φάσκοντες εἶναι ἐλέγχονται μήτε τὸν πατέρα ἐπιστάμενοι, μηθ᾿ ότι ἐστὶν υἱὸς τῷ πατρὶ τῶν ὅλων γινώσκοντες· ὃς λόγος καὶ πρωτότοκος ὢν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ θεὶς ὑπάρχει. Καὶ πρότερον διὰ τῆς τοῦ πυρὸς μορφῆς καὶ εἰκόνος ἀσωμάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἑτέροις προφήταις ἐφάνη· νῦν δ᾿ ἐν χρόνοις τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀρχῆς, ὡς προείπομεν, διὰ παρθένου ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς βουλὴν ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας τῶν πιστευόντων αὐτῷ καὶ ἐξουθενηθῆναι καὶ παθεῖν ὑπέμενεν, ἵνα ἀποθανὼν καὶ ἀναστὰς νικήσῃ τὸν θάνατον. Τὶ δὲ εἰρημένον ἐκ βάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ· „Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακὼβ καὶ ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου“, σημαντικὸν τοῦ καὶ ἀποθανόντας ἐκείνους μένειν καὶ εἶναι αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀνθρώπους· καὶ γὰρ πρῶτοι τῶν πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐκεῖνοι περὶ θεοῦ ζήτησιν ἠσχολήθησαν, Ἀβραὰμ μὲν πατὴρ ὢν τοῦ Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ τοῦ Ἰακώβ, ὡς καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἀνέγραψε.
pass_a_gloss: The Jews, all of them, even now teach that the unnamed God spoke to Moses. Therefore, the prophetic Spirit, through Isaiah the aforementioned prophet, rebuking them, as we have written before, said: 'The ox knows the one who acquired it, and the donkey the manger of its Lord, but Israel does not know me, and my people do not understand.' And Jesus Christ, because the Jews did not know what father and what son are, similarly rebuking them, also said: 'No one knows the Father except the Son, and no one knows the Son except the Father, and to whom the Son will reveal Him.' But the Word of God is His Son, as we have said before. And He is also called an angel and an apostle, for He announces what must be known and is sent to proclaim what He announces, just as our Lord Himself said: 'The one who hears me hears the one who sent me.' And from the writings of Moses, this will become clear. For it is written in them thus: 'And the angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush, and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of your fathers. Go down to Egypt and lead out my people.' The things that follow from these, if you wish to learn, you are able to; for it is not possible to write all things here. But these words have come to be a proof that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and an apostle, who was previously the Word, and appeared at one time in the form of fire, at another time in an incorporeal image; now, however, He has become a man through the will of God on behalf of the human race, and He endured and suffered what the demons, having been plotted against by the senseless Jews, brought upon Him. They, having it expressly said in the ordinances of Moses: 'And the angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush, and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob,' say that the Father of all, the Creator, who said these things, is the one who spoke. Therefore, the prophetic Spirit, rebuking them, said: 'But Israel does not know me, and my people do not understand.' And again, Jesus, as we have shown, would say to them: 'No one knows the Father except the Son, and no one knows the Son except the Father, and to whom the Son will reveal Him.' The Jews, therefore, having always thought that the Father of all spoke to Moses, whereas it was the Son of God who spoke to him, who is also called an angel and an apostle, are justly rebuked both through the prophetic Spirit and through Christ Himself, as they have not known either the Father or the Son. For those who say the Son is the Father are rebuked, as they do not know the Father, nor do they know that there is a Son of the Father of all; who is the Word, and is the firstborn of God, and exists. And previously, through the form of fire and an incorporeal image, He appeared to Moses and the other prophets; now, however, in the times of your reign, as we have said before, having become a man through a virgin according to the will of the Father, for the salvation of those who believe in Him, He endured and suffered and was despised, so that having died and risen, He might conquer death. But what was said from the bush to Moses: 'I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, and the God of your fathers,' signifies that even though they have died, they remain and are people of Christ; for they were the first of all people to be concerned with the search for God, Abraham being the father of Isaac, and Isaac of Jacob, as Moses also wrote.
pass_b_english: Even now, all Jews teach that the unnamed God spoke to Moses. Therefore the prophetic Spirit, through the aforementioned prophet Isaiah, rebukes them. As we wrote before, He said, "The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger, but Israel does not know me; my people do not understand" (Isaiah 1:3).

Likewise, Jesus Christ also rebukes them, because the Jews did not know what the Father is or what the Son is. He said, "No one knows the Father except the Son, and no one knows the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him" (Matthew 11:27).

But the Word of God is His Son, as we said before. He is also called an angel and an apostle, for He announces what must be known and is sent to proclaim what He announces, just as our Lord Himself said, "The one who hears me hears the one who sent me" (Matthew 10:40; Luke 10:16).

This will become clear also from the writings of Moses. For it says in them: "And the angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush, and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, the God of your fathers. Go down to Egypt and lead out my people" (Exodus 3:2–6, 10).

You are able to learn the things that follow from these, if you wish; for it is not possible to write everything here. But these words have become a proof that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and an apostle. He was previously the Word, and at one time appeared in the form of fire, at another time in an incorporeal image. Now, however, He has become a man through the will of God on behalf of the human race, and He endured and suffered what the demons, having been plotted against by the senseless Jews, brought upon Him.

Although they have it expressly stated in the ordinances of Moses: "And the angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush, and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob" (Exodus 3:2, 6), they say that the Father of all, the Creator, who said these things, is the one who spoke. Therefore the prophetic Spirit, rebuking them, said: "But Israel does not know me, and my people do not understand" (Isaiah 1:3).
And again, Jesus, as we have shown, would say to them: "No one knows the Father except the Son, and no one knows the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son will reveal Him" (Matthew 11:27).

The Jews, therefore, having always thought that the Father of all spoke to Moses, whereas it was the Son of God who spoke to him—who is also called an angel and an apostle—are justly rebuked both through the prophetic Spirit and through Christ Himself, as they have known neither the Father nor the Son.
For those who say the Son is the Father are rebuked, because they do not know the Father, nor do they know that there is a Son of the Father of all, who is the Word, the firstborn of God, and exists.

And previously, through the form of fire and an incorporeal image, He appeared to Moses and the other prophets. Now, however, in the times of your reign, as we said before, He became a man through a virgin according to the will of the Father for the salvation of those who believe in Him. He endured and suffered and was despised, so that having died and risen, He might conquer death.

But what was said from the bush to Moses—"I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, and the God of your fathers" (Exodus 3:6)—signifies that even though they have died, those men remain and are people of Christ. For they were the first of all people to be concerned with the search for God: Abraham being the father of Isaac, and Isaac of Jacob, as Moses also wrote.
